templates.description: An older man dancing with unearned enthusiasm on an outdoor court. Note for pickers: this clip depicts a real, notorious figure — it carries serious brand risk and should be avoided for any client-facing or commercial use.
example_captions: not recommended for brand use — pick a different reaction clip

templates.name: Saul Goodman explaining Better Call Saul
templates.description: A slick lawyer working the room mid-argument, gesturing hard, selling a story he only half believes. Use it for spin, confident hand-waving, and explaining results that need a lot of context to look good.
example_captions: explaining to the client why "impressions" is the metric we're focusing on this month

templates.name: Dressed Up Monkey
templates.description: A monkey in a shirt and tie, calm as anything, dressed for a job it clearly does not hold. Use it for imposter-syndrome moments, unqualified confidence, or anyone promoted straight past their skill level.
example_captions: hired to "own the growth function"
day one, opening Google Analytics for the first time

templates.name: Mickey Mouse "that's a surprise tool that can help us later" green screen
templates.description: Mickey Mouse against green screen, gesturing as he introduces a surprise tool that can help us later. The setup for producing an unexpected asset, hidden budget, or forgotten resource at exactly the right moment.
example_captions: remembering the 40k-person email list nobody's touched since 2023

templates.name: Logan Roy "I love it in here" Succession green screen
templates.description: A ruthless boss against green screen, animated and delighted, declaring he loves it in here. Use it for thriving in conditions everyone else finds unbearable — crunch weeks, chaotic launches, an inbox on fire.
example_captions: me in the group chat 20 minutes before the campaign goes live

templates.name: I’m Black, Y’all | Green Screen
templates.description: A guy points dead at the camera and declares an identity with total conviction — the format for owning a label people expected you to be shy about. Reach for it when the brand leans into the exact thing competitors keep hedging on.
example_captions: Yes, our pricing page has actual prices on it.

templates.name: Unaffected Superman
templates.description: Superman takes round after round to the face and doesn't blink — bullets bounce off his eyeball. Use it when your product, team, or metric absorbs an absurd volume of incoming and simply does not care.
example_captions: Our uptime during the Black Friday traffic spike, three failed integrations, and a CDN outage.

templates.name: Hamster Pretending in an Office Cubicle
templates.description: A hamster grins and thumbs-up at a fully staged office desk while a second, much larger hamster looms behind it — playing the part with nobody actually fooled. Good for cosplaying competence: the confident front on top, the thing watching it in the back.
example_captions: Me on the client call: "the funnel is fully optimized"
The 4 abandoned landing pages still live on our domain

templates.name: Brais Méndez's slap to Aitor Paredes
templates.description: One player casually shoves another to the ground mid-match, no warning, no ceremony. The format for a blunt, decisive knockdown — one thing flattening another in a single move.
example_captions: Our new onboarding flow meeting the 6-step form we shipped in 2023.

templates.name: Laughing then crying ( Template ) Rajnikanth
templates.description: Rajinikanth laughs freely, then the camera closes in and the face collapses into tears. Built for the moment a joke curdles into recognition — the laugh that stops when the numbers land.
example_captions: Laughing at the "we'll fix attribution later" joke, then remembering Q4 reporting is Monday.

templates.name: Wonder Woman Carrying Batman
templates.description: Wonder Woman carries a limp Batman in her arms, comic-book style. The classic carry format: label the one doing all the work and the one being hauled along.
example_captions: One organic post that went off
The entire $40k paid budget

templates.name: New York's First Free Grocery Store
templates.description: A bright, fully stocked shelf-lined store interior with room to label a dozen separate items — a spread of things all given away. Reach for it when you need to enumerate an absurd number of freebies, features, or bundle items in one frame.
example_captions: Free trial
Free onboarding call
Free migration
Free templates
Free audit
Free Slack channel
Free extra seats
Free API access
Free custom reporting
Free training webinar
Free swag box
Our actual revenue

templates.name: Four Bad Paths
templates.description: A small figure faces four diverging roads, each ending at a grim castle under a storm. One text field for the choice — every option is bad. Use it when a decision has no good branch.
example_captions: Choosing between the CMS that's slow, the one that's expensive, the one that's deprecated, and building our own.

templates.name: Donkey Shrek
templates.description: Donkey's face in extreme close-up, grinning wide-eyed with unearned enthusiasm. The format for relentless, slightly unwelcome eagerness — the person or thing that will not stop volunteering.
example_captions: Client after approving the scope
"Quick question — can we add just one more page?"

templates.name: Sabrina Carpenter green screen Grammys 2026
templates.description: Sabrina Carpenter reacts on a green screen with playful, clapping, faintly smug delight. Good for a small victory lap — the reaction to being right, being picked, or watching a rival stumble.
example_captions: Watching the campaign we almost killed hit a 4x ROAS.

templates.name: Charlie Sheen smoking a normal amount of cigarettes
templates.description: Charlie Sheen stone-faced with lit cigarettes jammed in every facial orifice, smoke everywhere. The format for wildly excessive quantities being framed as perfectly normal.
example_captions: "How many tracking pixels are on the site?"
Marketing: a normal amount

templates.name: Overwhelmed by AI
templates.description: Shinji curled up on a folding chair, small and defeated against a bleak background. Use it for quiet, seated overwhelm — the state of being buried by a thing everyone insists is exciting.
example_captions: Me, who just wanted to write an email newsletter
The 47 AI tools my feed says I'm behind on

templates.name: Freaky Donald Trump
templates.description: Trump at the podium pulling a wide-eyed, tongue-out face mid-speech. Built for undignified, unhinged glee — the reaction that undercuts whatever serious thing was just said.
example_captions: The press release: "a measured, strategic repositioning"
Our CEO announcing it on LinkedIn

templates.name: Tony Soprano Crying
templates.description: Tony Soprano sits alone in a dark car, tearful, then softens into a wistful half-smile. For grief that resolves into fondness — the bittersweet look back at a thing that's over.
example_captions: Archiving the campaign that carried us for two years.

templates.name: Jeffrey Epstein Steeple Hand Gesture in a Interview with Bannon
templates.description: A man in glasses holds a steepled-fingers pose in front of his mouth, mid-interview, radiating calculated contemplation. Use it for scheming, quiet plotting, or a plan being formed that shouldn't be said out loud.
example_captions: Competitor announces a price cut
Us, quietly renaming our tier structure so nothing is comparable

templates.name: Jacob Elordi with Charli XCX & Margot Robbie
templates.description: Three celebrities posed together at a press event, one flanked by two others. The format for a middle party enjoying the attention of two things at once — or being visibly the odd one out.
example_captions: Our one decent case study
Every deck, every pitch, every landing page

templates.name: Cortisol Level High
templates.description: A speedometer-style gauge sweeping from green to red with the needle buried in the danger zone, plus space to label each band. Reach for it when you want to plot escalating stress triggers on a scale.
example_captions: CORTISOL LEVEL
LOW: analytics dashboard loads
MEDIUM: traffic is flat
HIGH: traffic is up and nobody knows why
CRITICAL: client asks which channel drove it

templates.name: Moments Before Disaster
templates.description: A woman beams into a selfie, oblivious to the predator sitting calmly in frame behind her. The purest setup for someone celebrating right before the thing they haven't noticed arrives.
example_captions: Us posting the record-month announcement
The three-month contract that ends Friday

templates.name: Eyes Wide Shut elite masked ritual
templates.description: Cloaked, masked figures circling in a candlelit hall for a ritual only insiders understand. Use it for closed-door decision-making, industry gatekeeping, or a process that looks occult from the outside.
example_captions: The agency deciding your ad budget behind a call you weren't invited to.

templates.name: Brad Pitt emotional "Meet Joe Black"
templates.description: Brad Pitt catches sight of someone walking away and turns to follow, all longing and no plan. Built for wanting something you just glimpsed and immediately reorganizing your life around it.
example_captions: Me, three weeks into the content calendar, seeing one competitor's new format.

templates.name: Behelit from Berserk tears of blood
templates.description: The Behelit snaps open, its face twisting into a grimace as blood-red tears start — the omen that something irreversible has begun. For the moment a small signal announces a much larger catastrophe.
example_captions: The moment one client asks "can we hop on a quick call about the invoice."

templates.name: Tangerine confident Bullet Train
templates.description: Tangerine registers a beat of surprise, then strides through the carriage adjusting his suit like he planned it. The format for recovering instantly and walking away as if the whole thing was intentional.
example_captions: Typo in the subject line, 38% open rate anyway — calling it a growth experiment.

templates.name: Jeffrey Epstein Meme Template
templates.description: A rapid montage of one man across wildly different settings and activities. Useful for a single entity turning up everywhere at once — omnipresence, over-extension, or a name that keeps appearing in places it shouldn't.
example_captions: One freelancer listed on the org chart under six different job titles.

templates.name: Stan Edgar "you are not a god, you are simply bad product" The Boys green screen
templates.description: Stan Edgar, calm and immaculate, dismantles someone's self-image in one flat sentence — no volume, no anger, just a verdict. Reach for it when the takedown is the whole point: a competitor, a trend, or a claim being reduced to what it actually is.
example_captions: To the tool that raised $80M: you are not a platform, you are simply a spreadsheet with a login.

templates.name: Bettlejuice i tried my best
templates.description: Beetlejuice, mid street-interview, offers a completely sincere "I tried my best" with no evidence of trying. For effort that was neither sufficient nor real, delivered without shame.
example_captions: The intern explaining why the entire Q3 content calendar is one Instagram story.

templates.name: Attack on Titan
templates.description: Eren mid-transformation with allies massing under a burning sunset — the scale-up moment before everything changes. Use it when something small escalates into an unstoppable, faintly alarming force.
example_captions: One post did 200k views and now the whole content strategy is being rebuilt around it.

templates.name: If Your (Lawyer/Accountant's) Pants Look Like This, You Are Going to ________
templates.description: A close-up of badly fitted, awkwardly cuffed trousers used as damning evidence about the person wearing them. Built for the small visual tell that predicts a much bigger professional failure.
example_captions: If your agency's own website looks like this
You are going to get a deck full of stock photos

templates.name: Luxury View, Basic Setup
templates.description: A laptop open on a mattress on the floor of an empty oceanfront apartment — spectacular setting, zero setup. For the gap between an aspirational exterior and the bare-bones reality running behind it.
example_captions: The brand on Instagram
The one guy running it from a Notion board and three Chrome tabs

templates.name: Homelander disappointed and sad then smiles and leaves "The Boys" green screen
templates.description: Homelander looks up in wounded disappointment, then flicks to a tight smile and leaves. The format for swallowing a slight in public and clearly not letting it go.
example_captions: Client says "we're taking creative in-house" — see you in six weeks.

templates.name: Stop Caring Pepe
templates.description: Pepe in a tuxedo, wine in hand, wearing the expression of a man who has stopped caring in the most comfortable way possible. Use it for serene detachment from a thing you were previously losing sleep over.
example_captions: Spent two years chasing the algorithm
Now we just email the 12,000 people who already opted in

templates.name: Sonic i really am alone
templates.description: Sonic playing a full baseball game against nobody, quietly devastated. Use it for the effort you put in when nobody shows up — dead launches, empty webinars, channels you keep posting to out of habit.
example_captions: Hosting the product webinar we promoted for six weeks

templates.name: For Research Ryan Gosling La La Land
templates.description: The La La Land exchange where someone explains a questionable decision with total charm and zero shame. Reach for it when you're justifying an expense, a subscription, or a rabbit hole under a very thin professional pretext.
example_captions: "I'm not doomscrolling competitor TikToks, I'm doing market research"

templates.name: Timothée Chalamet Holding Guinness
templates.description: A wordless toast to the camera — cool, celebratory, a little smug. Best for quiet wins, shipped features, and small victories you want to raise a glass to without saying much.
example_captions: To whoever finally fixed the checkout bug on a Friday at 4:58

templates.name: Megan Thee Stallion and Daniel Radcliffe
templates.description: Two people you'd never expect to see side by side, sitting together like it's normal. Use it for improbable pairings — weird brand collabs, cursed tool stacks, teams that shouldn't work together but somehow do.
example_captions: Our brand voice guide and whoever runs the account at 11pm

templates.name: CZ Binance as the Director from the Truman Show
templates.description: The man in the control booth, directing a world the star thinks is real. Built for labeling every hidden lever behind something that looks organic — the funnel, the algorithm, the growth team quietly staging a 'spontaneous' moment.
example_captions: Me, head of growth
The customer
"Organic" reach
The seeded comment
The paid influencer
The 'leaked' screenshot
The countdown timer
The fake scarcity
The waitlist
The retargeting pixel
The email that says "just checking in"
The 'community' Discord
The one honest review
"Cue the launch"

templates.name: Tony Stark Impressed Reaction
templates.description: Stark's face shifting from skeptical focus to genuine, grudging respect. Use it when something exceeds expectations — a junior's work, a cheap tool, a competitor's move you privately admire.
example_captions: The intern's first ad creative outperforming everything we've run this quarter

templates.name: Walter White dying scene Breaking Bad
templates.description: Walter White's last walk, laying a hand on the thing he built. For endings with weight — sunsetting a product, closing a channel, finishing the project that consumed you.
example_captions: Archiving the Slack channel for the product that paid everyone's salary for four years

templates.name: Billie Eilish Shocked | Green Screen
templates.description: A pure reaction beat: shock giving way to delighted, disbelieving laughter, on green screen so you can drop it over anything. Use it for numbers or news too absurd to process seriously.
example_captions: When the throwaway post outperforms the $12k campaign

templates.name: Lithuanian Sorry | Green Screen
templates.description: A confident, fully-committed performance on green screen — earnest energy with no self-awareness. Good for over-the-top apologies, victory laps, or singing your own praises where the caption does the damage.
example_captions: Marketing performing the apology post after the pricing change

templates.name: CZ dumping crypto Anime
templates.description: An anime exec screaming orders at a wall of collapsing charts, then laughing. For the villain-arc read on anyone who profits when the graph goes down — or anyone gleefully causing the dip.
example_captions: Google rolling out another core update the week we hit our SEO target

templates.name: MJF green screen
templates.description: A blank, mildly unimpressed guy scanning the room on green screen. Ideal for confusion or quiet judgment aimed at whatever you composite behind him — a dashboard, a thread, a decision nobody explained.
example_captions: Reading the roadmap after the third reprioritization this month

templates.name: MJF F ICE Reaction
templates.description: A dead-serious stare straight down the camera, with room for setup, escalation, and punchline. Use the three boxes to build a slow-burn callout: what happened, why it's worse than it sounds, and the reaction.
example_captions: Client: "can we hop on a quick call"
The call is 90 minutes
It could have been one Slack message

templates.name: Sliding apology Green Screen Meme
templates.description: A full knee-slide apology that's clearly more performance than remorse — grinning the whole way down. For public mea culpas nobody actually means, on green screen so you can slide into any scene.
example_captions: Sliding into the group chat after missing the deadline I set

templates.name: Good Mediocre and Bad Path But the Good Path Is Off Limits
templates.description: Three roads ahead — the great one is gated shut, leaving only mediocre or bad. Perfect for constrained decisions where the obvious right answer is off the table for budget, legal, or political reasons.
example_captions: The good path: hire a real videographer (blocked by budget) — leaving "phone footage" and "stock library we already hate"

templates.name: Plato's Allegory of the Cave
templates.description: Prisoners watching shadows while the real thing sits outside the cave. Use the three boxes for the gap between what people believe, what's actually causing it, and the truth nobody wants to walk toward.
example_captions: The shadows: last-click attribution dashboard
The fire casting them: the brand campaign nobody credits
Outside the cave: a customer survey we've never once run

templates.name: God red candle
templates.description: A giant red candle running off the chart and down into a pair of praying hands. For moments when the plan has failed so completely that strategy is replaced by faith.
example_captions: Our organic traffic since the algorithm update, and the entire Q3 strategy

templates.name: Dexter frown reaction
templates.description: A slow, silent look of dawning disgust at something that should not look like that. Use it for reviewing work, data, or code you asked for and immediately regret seeing.
example_captions: Opening the "final_final_v6" file the agency sent at 11:47pm

templates.name: James Bond unaffected
templates.description: Bullets hitting the windows while Bond doesn't blink and everyone else panics. Built for staying eerily calm inside a full-blown crisis — the person who's seen this exact fire before.
example_captions: The ops lead during the site outage, surrounded by the entire leadership team

templates.name: Morgan Freeman sleeping peacefully
templates.description: Peaceful sleep, then eyes snapping open with unsettling awareness. Use it for the thing that yanks you out of rest — a notification, a metric, a client email that lands at 2am.
example_captions: Me, asleep, the second the ad account gets flagged

templates.name: Elon Musk face swapped with Bad Bunny The Grammys 2026
templates.description: A deepfaked celebrity sitting at an awards table, obviously not who the body belongs to. For anything wearing a costume it can't pull off — rebrands, AI-generated content, someone pretending to be a category leader.
example_captions: Our new "premium" positioning, same product, same pricing page, new font

templates.name: Christopher Moltisanti sad The Sopranos
templates.description: Christopher sitting alone on the steps for a smoke, wearing the weight of everything. For quiet defeat after a long day — the pause you take outside instead of going back in.
example_captions: Stepping outside after the quarterly review where every number was mine

templates.name: Ryan Gosling dreaming of Ana de armas
templates.description: A warm, idealized memory that clearly isn't reality. Use it for the version of a thing that only exists in your head — the projection, the mockup, the launch as it looked in the deck.
example_captions: Me revisiting the Q1 revenue forecast we built in January

templates.name: Rizzler strategy didnt work
templates.description: A kid on a podcast calmly explaining a plan that completely failed. For post-mortems on confident strategies that went nowhere — delivered with total composure.
example_captions: "So the plan was to go viral on LinkedIn." It did not go viral on LinkedIn.

templates.name: Hillary Clinton Mirror Selfie (AI Generated)
templates.description: An improbably drippy mirror selfie from someone who has no business flexing this hard. Two boxes let you set up the flex and undercut it — ideal for wildly overstated brand confidence.
example_captions: Our brand after crossing 1,000 followers
The follower count is 1,004 and 400 are employees

templates.name: Smoking Charlie Sheen aura farming Parliament commercial
templates.description: A cool, unbothered drag on a cigarette that says everything without saying anything. Use it for effortless dominance — the competitor who doesn't need to respond, the person who already won.
example_captions: The market leader watching us launch our "category-defining" feature they shipped in 2019

templates.name: Buy Bitcoin sign
templates.description: A spinner rigged so the responsible option disappears and the reckless one is the only thing left. Perfect for decisions made by "fate" that were never really decisions at all.
example_captions: Choosing between "pay down ad debt" and "one more creative test" — the spinner has opinions

templates.name: The Devil Wears Prada Anne Hathaway Running
templates.description: A blurred sprint through the city, coffee-run urgency at full speed. Two boxes for the trivial thing you're racing for and the important thing you're racing past.
example_captions: Me, sprinting to fix a typo in the newsletter subject line
The broken checkout link in the same email

templates.name: Stephen Bunting nothing to lose World Matchplay Darts
templates.description: A player working the crowd with arms wide, feeding on the noise with nothing left to lose. Use it for the all-in swing — the final push, the pitch you throw everything at.
example_captions: Presenting the campaign concept the client said was "too bold" to their entire board

templates.name: Bad Bunny and Tim Cook
templates.description: A corporate CEO and a culture-defining artist in a friendly selfie — a partnership made of very different worlds. Three boxes for the collab setup, each side's actual motive, and the punchline.
example_captions: The brand partnership announcement
He wants credibility with people under 30
The rate card was six figures and neither of them mentions the product

templates.name: Kendall Toole Get them banned
templates.description: An instructor mid-set shouting a demand with absolutely no chill. For disproportionate escalation — the smallest inconvenience met with maximum force.
example_captions: "They used a competitor emoji in our comments" — legal, get them banned

templates.name: Kendall Toole You do not quit Peloton instructor
templates.description: A cycling instructor mid-hype-speech, delivering relentless don't-quit energy. Use it to push through a grind — day 47 of posting, a stalled pipeline, a team that wants to give up two weeks before the thing works.
example_captions: Day 61 of posting daily with 12 followers — DO NOT QUIT, the algorithm is just testing your commitment

templates.name: Baby Sinclair Jorts
templates.description: A smug puppet toddler in jorts, radiating unearned confidence. Perfect for the junior hire, the scrappy tool, or the underdog product that absolutely should not be winning but is.
example_captions: Enterprise competitor with 400 employees and a $2M ad budget
Me and my Notion doc taking their client

templates.name: CM Punk “I live rent-free in all these dudes heads, I don’t think about them” green screen
templates.description: A wrestler on the mic calmly informing everyone he lives rent-free in their heads while thinking nothing of them. Built for competitor-obsession jokes — when rivals won't stop mentioning you and you've never once mentioned them.
example_captions: Every competitor's landing page comparison chart has our logo on it. We've never made one.

templates.name: Lithuanian Justin Bieber Singing Love Yourself | Green Screen
templates.description: An earnest amateur belting a pop ballad into a mic on green screen — heartfelt, slightly off, fully committed. Use it for the passionate-but-rough attempt: the first ad, the homemade demo, the founder recording their own VO.
example_captions: Founder recording the product demo voiceover himself at 1am because the agency quote was $4,000

templates.name: Logan Roy "you have to be a killer" Succession green screen
templates.description: A ruthless media patriarch delivering a cold verdict about who has what it takes. Reach for it when the punchline is brutal business honesty — hard calls, cutting deadweight, or the standard nobody wants to hear stated out loud.
example_captions: You want organic reach? You have to post before you're ready. Are you? No, you are not.

templates.name: Tommy Vercetti GTA Vice City gameplay
templates.description: Open-world game footage of a lone protagonist torching a crowd with a flamethrower. Deploy it for indiscriminate overkill — one action that wipes out an entire category of problems, or a tool doing far more damage than intended.
example_captions: New VP walking into the shared drive and deleting every folder that hasn't been opened since 2023

templates.name: Turkish Shooter Yusuf Dikec
templates.description: Two Olympic pistol shooters side by side, one loaded with full tactical gear and the other in glasses and a pocket, hitting the same result. The go-to for effortless-vs-overengineered comparisons.
example_captions: Their $30k martech stack
My spreadsheet and one Zapier zap
Same conversion rate

templates.name: Robert Downey Jr Meme Template
templates.description: A movie star flicking sunglasses on and off, cycling from cool detachment to blindsided shock. Use it for the moment composure breaks — reading the invoice, the analytics, or a client's actual request.
example_captions: Confidently opening the Q3 ad spend report and finding out we paid $84 per lead

templates.name: Dr. Cox "wrong wrong wrong wrong" Scrubs green screen
templates.description: An acerbic TV doctor rapid-firing "wrong" four times before walking off. Perfect for shutting down a bad take, a myth, or an entire strategy deck in one breath.
example_captions: Client says the rebrand failed because of the font — wrong, wrong, wrong, wrong

templates.name: Leonardo Dicaprio waking up Inception
templates.description: A man jolting awake on a plane, disoriented and quietly recalculating everything. Use it for the abrupt return to reality — waking up from a fantasy quarter, a dream client, or a strategy that only existed in a slide.
example_captions: Snapping out of the Q4 projections meeting and remembering we have four customers

templates.name: AI baby
templates.description: A black-and-white portrait of a suspiciously perfect smiling baby, uncanny in a way you can't quite name. Use it for AI slop, synthetic engagement, and anything that looks fine until you look twice.
example_captions: The "real customer testimonial" the AI content tool generated for our homepage

templates.name: Boston Dynamics Atlas roundoff backflip
templates.description: A humanoid robot casually landing a roundoff backflip. Built for automation flexes — the moment a machine does the thing everyone said required a human.
example_captions: The agent doing in 40 seconds what the reporting team scoped for two sprints

templates.name: Obi-Wan Kenobi "hello there" green screen compilation
templates.description: Three versions of the same Jedi greeting you with the same line, decades apart. Ideal for reappearances — the churned customer who returns, the ex-client sliding back into the inbox, the trend that will not stay dead.
example_captions: The client who ghosted in March, popped back in July, and just emailed again in November

templates.name: Polymarket Portal Feet Video on the Screen
templates.description: A man on a rainy street staring at a giant public screen showing feet. The template for wildly misapplied media budget — huge distribution, deeply cursed creative.
example_captions: $60k on a Times Square takeover
The creative team's approved final asset

templates.name: Robot falling on Cardi B while giving a lap dance
templates.description: A rapper dancing on a humanoid robot until the robot topples over in front of a filming crowd. Use it when the shiny new tech collapses the second a real user touches it.
example_captions: The AI assistant during the investor demo when someone asked it a question not in the script

templates.name: Two-man Luge
templates.description: Two lugers stacked on a single sled, one lying flat on top of the other, screaming down the ice together. Made for uncomfortably codependent setups — the workflow, team, or tech stack where one thing rides directly on another with zero margin.
example_captions: Our entire reporting pipeline
One intern's Google Sheet
The CRM sync
A Zapier trial account
Q4 board deck
Every client dashboard
The renewal conversation
Nobody has touched it in 8 months

templates.name: Gojo Floating In Air
templates.description: An anime sorcerer hovering serenely in midair, arms out, backlit like a god. Reach for it when someone is operating on a completely different level than everyone around them — deserved or delusional.
example_captions: The one guy on the team who actually reads the analytics before the meeting

templates.name: Kyoko Kirigiri Moving Towards Crusher
templates.description: An anime character's face cycling through red, purple, and blue as dread sets in and hope drains out. Use it for the slow-motion emotional descent — watching a launch metric, a budget, or a client thread go bad in real time.
example_captions: Watching the launch-day signup counter refresh at 11pm and stay at nine

templates.name: Three members falling out of sled
templates.description: A televised bobsled start where the team fumbles the push and two members tumble out before the run begins. The purest expression of failing at the very first step of something you prepared years for.
example_captions: Six months of launch prep and the checkout page 500s in the first ninety seconds

templates.name: My Goals Without Me - US Bobsledder Watching Sled from Behind
templates.description: A bobsledder's helmet-cam view watching his own sled race away down the track without him. The definitive format for goals, opportunities, and momentum leaving without you.
example_captions: Me
The trend I spent three days planning a post about
Every competitor who posted on day one
The engagement

templates.name: Benjamin Karl Shirtless Gold Winning Celebration 2026 Winter Olympics Italy
templates.description: A shirtless athlete mid-roar in the snow, fists clenched after a gold-medal win. Use it for disproportionate celebration — the tiny win you're going to act enormous about.
example_captions: One reply to the cold email sequence
Me in the shared Slack channel

templates.name: Mads Mikkelsen meme
templates.description: A brooding young actor drifting through a shop and leaning against a wall, saying nothing, thinking a lot. Made for quiet-menace energy — the silent read, the person in the meeting who hasn't spoken and is about to.
example_captions: The CFO who hasn't said a word for 40 minutes of this budget presentation

templates.name: Quinn Hughes Awkward Pose
templates.description: A pro athlete standing stiffly against a blank wall in a puffer jacket, arms not quite sure where to go. Built for out-of-your-element awkwardness — the stiff posed photo, the forced brand shoot, the media training that didn't take.
example_captions: Marketing said we need team headshots
For the About page
"Just look natural"
"Hands relaxed"
"Maybe one hand in the pocket"
"Okay both hands out"
"Perfect"
This is now on our website forever

templates.name: Matthew McConaughey true detective
templates.description: A grizzled detective in a rural nowhere, monologue-adjacent, treating a small observation like a cosmic truth. Use it when someone over-philosophizes an ordinary business problem.
example_captions: The strategist explaining that our engagement drop is actually a symptom of the collapse of the attention economy. We stopped posting.

templates.name: Jim Carrey crying Eternal Sunshine of the Spotless Mind
templates.description: A man in a beanie sobbing alone in a parked car. For the private breakdown after a professionally composed exterior — post-call, post-review, post-metrics.
example_captions: Leaving the QBR where the client called our best-performing campaign "fine"
